pages.title: What is Analogy?
pages.body:
Analogy means a similarity or comparison between two pairs of things. In SSC CGL you are given a pair with a relationship, and you must find another pair (or a missing term) with the same relationship.

Core ideaIf A : B has relationship R, find C : D where the same R holds.
Doctor : Patient :: Teacher : Student — same relationship.

pages.title: Common Relationship Types
pages.body:
Recognising the type of relationship is the key skill. Here are the most common ones in SSC CGL:

RelationshipExample
Worker : Tool / ProductCarpenter : Wood :: Blacksmith : Iron
Animal : Young oneCow : Calf :: Dog : Puppy
Animal : DwellingLion : Den :: Bird : Nest
Whole : PartWheel : Car :: Page : Book
Symbol : QuantityOhm : Resistance :: Ampere : Current
Country : CapitalIndia : Delhi :: Japan : Tokyo
Word : SynonymBig : Large :: Small : Tiny
Word : AntonymHot : Cold :: Light : Dark
Degree (intensity)Warm : Hot :: Cool : Cold
Cause : EffectFire : Ash :: Rain : Flood
Study : SubjectCardiology : Heart :: Entomology : Insects
Male : FemaleTiger : Tigress :: Lion : Lioness
StrategyAlways frame the relationship in a full sentence: "A doctor treats a patient". Then check which option fits the same sentence.

pages.title: Question Formats & Worked Examples
pages.body:
Format 1 — Complete the pair

5 : 36 :: 6 : ?
Pattern: n : (n+1)². So 5 → 36, 6 → 7² = 49. Answer: 49.
Book : Author :: Painting : ?
An author writes a book; a painter paints a painting. Answer: Painter.

Format 2 — Choose the analogous pair

Given "Museum : Curator", which pair is analogous?
Relationship: official in charge of a place. Options like "Library : Librarian" fit. Pick the pair where the second manages/cares-for the first.

Format 3 — Number analogies

8 : 64 :: 9 : ?
8² = 64, so 9² = 81. Answer: 81.
3 : 27 :: 4 : ?
3³ = 27, so 4³ = 64. Answer: 64.
Negative-marking reminderAnalogy questions are usually quick wins in Tier-I (1 mark after +2/−0.5 is good EV if you're >60% confident). But obscure vocabulary analogies are traps — skip if you genuinely don't know the words.

pages.title: Letter-Based Analogies
pages.body:
Letters are treated by their position in the alphabet (A=1, B=2, …, Z=26). A common trick: convert letters to numbers and look for the pattern.

AC : FH :: KM : ?
AC → positions 1,3. FH → 6,8. Difference +5,+5. KM → 11,13; add 5,5 → 16,18 = PR. Answer: PR.
ADG : GDA :: CFI : ?
Reverse the order: CFI reversed = IFC. Answer: IFC.
Quick alphabet tipRemember EJOTY (5,10,15,20,25) and the position of M(13)/N(14) as the halfway marks to count faster.

practice.question: Doctor : Patient :: Teacher : ?
practice.explanation: A doctor treats a patient; a teacher teaches a student.

practice.question: Book : Author :: Painting : ?
practice.explanation: An author creates a book; a painter creates a painting.

practice.question: Cow : Calf :: Dog : ?
practice.explanation: Calf is the young of a cow; puppy is the young of a dog.

practice.question: Lion : Den :: Bird : ?
practice.explanation: A lion lives in a den; a bird lives in a nest.

practice.question: Wheel : Car :: Page : ?
practice.explanation: A wheel is part of a car; a page is part of a book (part : whole).

practice.question: Ohm : Resistance :: Ampere : ?
practice.explanation: Ohm is the unit of resistance; ampere is the unit of current.

practice.question: India : Delhi :: Japan : ?
practice.explanation: Delhi is the capital of India; Tokyo is the capital of Japan.

practice.question: Hot : Cold :: Light : ?
practice.explanation: Antonyms: hot/cold, light/dark.

practice.question: Cardiology : Heart :: Entomology : ?
practice.explanation: Cardiology is the study of the heart; entomology is the study of insects.

practice.question: Tiger : Tigress :: Lion : ?
practice.explanation: Male : female form. Tigress is female tiger; lioness is female lion.

practice.question: Carpenter : Wood :: Blacksmith : ?
practice.explanation: A carpenter works with wood; a blacksmith works with iron.

practice.question: AC : FH :: KM : ?
practice.explanation: Letter positions: AC(1,3), FH(6,8) add 5,5. KM(11,13) + 5,5 = 16,18 = PR.
Pattern: n : n x (n+1). 4 x 5 = 20, so 6 x 7 = 42.

practice.question: Fire : Ash :: Rain : ?
practice.explanation: Cause : effect. Fire produces ash; rain (in excess) produces flood.

practice.question: Knife : Cut :: Pen : ?
practice.explanation: Tool : function. A knife cuts; a pen writes.

practice.question: Petal : Flower :: Leaf : ?
practice.explanation: Part : whole. A petal is part of a flower; a leaf is part of a tree.

practice.question: Museum : Curator :: Library : ?
practice.explanation: A curator manages a museum; a librarian manages a library.
Pattern: n = a x b with a-b constant. 12 = 3x4, 20 = 4x5 (consecutive). 30 = 5x6, ? = 6x7 = 42.

practice.question: Warm : Hot :: Cool : ?
practice.explanation: Degree (intensified). Warm -> hot; cool -> cold.

practice.question: Captain : Team :: Pilot : ?
practice.explanation: A captain leads a team; a pilot leads a crew.

practice.question: AB : CD :: EF : ?
practice.explanation: Each letter shifts by +2: AB->CD, EF->GH.

practice.question: Peacock : India :: Kangaroo : ?
practice.explanation: National animal/bird : country. Peacock is India's; kangaroo is Australia's.

practice.question: Stethoscope : Doctor :: Gavel : ?
practice.explanation: Tool : user. A doctor uses a stethoscope; a judge uses a gavel.

practice.question: Earth : Planet :: Moon : ?
practice.explanation: Earth is a planet; the moon is a satellite.

practice.question: College : Student :: Hospital : ?
practice.explanation: A student is served by/attends a college; a patient is served by a hospital.

practice.question: Menu : Restaurant :: Catalogue : ?
practice.explanation: A menu lists a restaurant's offerings; a catalogue lists a store's offerings.

practice.question: Mountain : Hill :: River : ?
practice.explanation: Big : small of the same type. Mountain : hill; river : stream.

practice.question: Odometer : Speed :: Barometer : ?
practice.explanation: An odometer measures distance/speed; a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.
